assembly_instructions: 1. Lay the base_frame at y=0 and bolt the input_plate, embedding_table, token_flow_bus, and curriculum datum hardware to the left and rear edges; these establish the token stream width, V≈200K vocabulary datum, and 4M-context curriculum path. 2. Install the vertical residual_pipe through the centerline, then mount each stage as two split cutaway half-trays around the pipe so the spine remains visible: stage_01_left/right through stage_08_left/right represent eight 12-layer macrocycles. 3. Attach the 96-layer count comb beside the residual pipe: mount eight 12-layer macro teeth and align one blue softmax checkpoint bead to the top of each macrocycle. 4. Mount the exposed lightning branch on the front-left rail: lightning_pre_norm feeds lightning_qkv_gate_proj, then gated_lightning_scan_kernel, lightning_state_bank, and lightning_o_proj back into the residual pipe. 5. Mount the exposed softmax branch on the rear-left rail: softmax_qkv_proj feeds rope_rotary_unit, sliding_window_mask_4096, softmax_kv_cache_stack, and flash_attention_output back into the residual pipe. 6. Build the MoE module on the right: install moe_router above the residual tap, connect it to moe_dispatch_bus, sixteen visible routed expert cartridges arranged as a 4×4 detail view of the 64-expert bank, the moe_shared_expert, moe_combine_bus, expert_index_slab_64, fp4_weight_shelf, and the residual_return_bus. 7. Install the tied prediction_head and lm_loss_probe at the top of the residual pipe. 8. Add the MARS post-training loop above the model: mars_policy_swarm connects to reward_model_bank, rollout_buffer_200k, and optimizer_adamw_muon, with gradients returning through trainer_feedback_bus. 9. Add the parallelism_backplane and context_curriculum_pipe at the rear-right edge, tied by the parallelism_datum_bus, to document TP, EP, PP, DP, chunk-scan prefill, and the 4M-token curriculum. 10. Verify that every non-root part connects to base_frame directly or through residual_pipe, token_flow_bus, or a named support rail, and that no major subsystem is hidden inside an opaque enclosure.

info.summary: PROJECTED next-generation reasoning flagship from MiniMax, extrapolated from MiniMax-Text-01 → M1 research direction. No public paper at scene time. Best guess: pushes lightning attention further — 11:1 LIGHTNING:SOFTMAX ratio (was 7:1 in M1), learnable gating on the state update (Mamba-style), softmax replaced with sliding-window 4096 (full-context dropped). 96 layers, ~720B total / ~55B activated, 64 routed + 1 shared expert top-3 (was 32+1 top-2), 4M native input context, 200K output budget, post-trained with a projected MARS (Multi-Agent Reasoning with Self-play) RL successor to CISPO.
info.description:
MiniMax-M2.7 is presented here as a research-trajectory PROJECTION, not a paper. Where MiniMax-M1 was 7:1 lightning:softmax over 80 layers with full-context softmax and 32 experts top-2, M2.7 likely (i) PUSHES the lightning ratio to 11:1 — the M1 paper hinted that recall could be preserved with fewer softmax layers if the softmax is smarter, (ii) replaces full-context softmax with SLIDING-WINDOW softmax (4096-token window) — an operational simplification that bounds KV memory cleanly, (iii) adds LEARNABLE GATING to the lightning kernel (Mamba/Mamba-2 style decay) — measurably better long-range recall than fixed-feature-map linear attention, (iv) doubles routed-expert count (32 → 64) at top-3 (was top-2) for ~50% more active capacity, (v) extends native input context 1M → 4M with a multi-stage curriculum, (vi) succeeds CISPO with a projected 'MARS' (Multi-Agent Reasoning with Self-play) algorithm that matches multiple policies against each other on math/code/agent tasks.

Design rationale, in one line each:
• 11:1 lightning ratio: KV memory at 4M ctx is dominated almost entirely by the 8 softmax layers — and they only carry a 4096 window.
• Mamba-style gating: the single biggest reason linear attention finally matches softmax on long-range recall.
• Sliding-window softmax: bounds the KV cache regardless of input length — an operational win at 4M ctx.
• 64 experts top-3: more active capacity per token without proportionally growing all-to-all traffic.
• MARS RL: M1's CISPO solved long-rollout stability; the next problem is reasoning-via-debate and self-play.

facts.label: attention pattern
facts.value: 11 LIGHTNING gated-linear layers : 1 SOFTMAX sliding-window layer

facts.label: precision
facts.value: BF16 weights + projected FP4/FP8 expert GEMMs

comparisons.delta: Same family. Projected M2.7 grows: total params 456B → 720B, activated 45.9B → 55B. Layers move 80 → 96, lightning:softmax ratio moves 7:1 → 11:1, experts move 32 → 64, top-k moves 2 → 3, context moves 1M → 4M, and CISPO RL is projected forward into MARS RL.
Text-01 introduced the 7:1 hybrid; M2.7 keeps the hybrid idea but pushes gated linear attention, sliding-window softmax, deeper sparse MoE capacity, and reasoning-specific post-training.

parts.name: Open Assembly Base Frame
parts.role: Thin datum plate that grounds the whole schematic and prevents subsystems from appearing to float.

parts.name: Input Tokens Plate (V≈200K)
parts.role: Token-ID entry plate for the projected 200K-token vocabulary stream.

parts.name: Embedding Table (V≈200K, d=6144)
parts.role: Tied embedding and LM-head weight table; it maps token ids into the d=6144 residual stream.

parts.name: Token Flow Bus
parts.role: Visible input-to-residual conduit showing the assembly order from token ids through embeddings into the stack.

parts.name: Residual Stream Spine (d=6144)
parts.role: Central pre-norm residual carrier that every cutaway stage reads from and writes back to.

parts.name: 96-Layer Count Comb Spine
parts.role: Vertical ruler that carries eight separate 12-layer macro teeth for counting the full 96-layer depth.

parts.name: Macro Tooth 1: Layers 1-12
parts.role: Count mark for the first eleven lightning layers plus softmax layer 12.

parts.name: Macro Tooth 2: Layers 13-24
parts.role: Count mark for the second 12-layer hybrid macrocycle ending at softmax layer 24.

parts.name: Macro Tooth 3: Layers 25-36
parts.role: Count mark for the third 12-layer macrocycle ending at softmax layer 36.

parts.name: Macro Tooth 4: Layers 37-48
parts.role: Count mark for the fourth macrocycle and midpoint of the projected 96-layer stack.

parts.name: Macro Tooth 5: Layers 49-60
parts.role: Count mark for the fifth macrocycle showing the sparse softmax cadence continues after midpoint.

parts.name: Macro Tooth 6: Layers 61-72
parts.role: Count mark for the sixth 12-layer macrocycle ending at softmax layer 72.

parts.name: Macro Tooth 7: Layers 73-84
parts.role: Count mark for the seventh macrocycle ending at softmax layer 84.

parts.name: Macro Tooth 8: Layers 85-96
parts.role: Count mark for the final 12-layer macrocycle ending at layer 96.

parts.name: Stage 1 Right Cutaway Tray

parts.name: Stage 2 Right Cutaway Tray
parts.role: Right half of stage 2 aligned to the softmax checkpoint at layer 24.

parts.name: Stage 3 Left Cutaway Tray

parts.name: Stage 3 Right Cutaway Tray

parts.name: Stage 4 Right Cutaway Tray

parts.name: Stage 5 Right Cutaway Tray

parts.name: Stage 8 Right Cutaway Tray

parts.name: Exploded Lightning Branch Rail
parts.role: Open support rail holding the lightning sublayer pieces outside the stack so no internal part is hidden.

parts.name: Lightning Pre-RMSNorm
parts.role: Normalizes the residual stream before the gated linear-attention sublayer.

parts.name: Lightning QKV + Decay-Gate Projection
parts.role: Projects Q, K, V and the per-token learnable decay gate that controls state retention.

parts.name: Gated Lightning Scan Kernel
parts.role: Updates the recurrent state with a Mamba-style decay, giving constant-context memory with selective forgetting.
parts.memory_footprint: ≈ 1–2 MB recurrent state per sequence per layer

parts.name: Fixed-Size Lightning State Bank
parts.role: Ring-shaped state store showing that lightning memory is fixed-size and independent of the 4M-token input length.
parts.memory_footprint: constant in T; roughly MB-scale per layer per sequence

parts.name: Lightning Output Projection
parts.role: Projects the gated-lightning result back to the d=6144 residual width.

parts.name: Exploded Sliding-Softmax Branch Rail
parts.role: Open support rail for the sparse softmax pieces, placed behind the stack but visible from side and top views.

parts.name: Softmax QKV Projection (GQA 64Q/8KV)
parts.role: Generates grouped-query Q, K, and V tensors only for the eight periodic sliding-softmax layers.
parts.algorithm: Q,K,V = projections(x) with 64 Q heads and 8 KV heads

parts.name: RoPE Position Unit
parts.role: Applies rotary position embedding before the 4096-token causal window is evaluated.

parts.name: 4096-Token Sliding Window Mask
parts.role: Bounds softmax attention to the previous 4096 tokens, replacing full-context KV growth.

parts.name: Softmax KV Cache Stack
parts.role: Holds the eight-layer by 4096-token GQA KV cache, which stays bounded even at 4M input length.

parts.name: Sliding FlashAttention Output
parts.role: Computes the sparse softmax attention result and returns it to the residual stream.

parts.name: MoE Module Rail
parts.role: Right-side open rail carrying the router, experts, and all-to-all buses as an exposed assembly.

parts.name: Top-3 Softmax Router
parts.role: Chooses the top three routed experts from a projected bank of 64, with one shared expert always available.

parts.name: Expert Dispatch Bus
parts.role: NCCL all-to-all dispatch path that sends token batches to the selected expert shards.

parts.name: Routed Expert Cartridge 1 of 64
parts.role: Visible cartridge for one SwiGLU routed expert with d_ff≈9216 in the 64-expert bank.

parts.name: Routed Expert Cartridge 2 of 64
parts.role: Visible cartridge for a second independently routed expert shard.

parts.name: Routed Expert Cartridge 3 of 64
parts.role: Visible cartridge that can be one of the top-3 experts selected by the router.

parts.name: Routed Expert Cartridge 4 of 64
parts.role: Visible cartridge proving the MoE is a bank of separate FFN shards, not a dense block.

parts.name: Routed Expert Cartridge 5 of 64
parts.role: Second-row routed expert cartridge showing expert parallel placement across devices.

parts.name: Routed Expert Cartridge 6 of 64
parts.role: Second-row routed expert cartridge for a separate shard in the all-to-all path.

parts.name: Routed Expert Cartridge 7 of 64
parts.role: Second-row routed expert cartridge that receives a capacity-limited token batch.

parts.name: Routed Expert Cartridge 8 of 64
parts.role: Second-row routed expert cartridge completing the front half of the exposed 16-expert detail.

parts.name: Routed Expert Cartridge 9 of 64
parts.role: Rear-row expert cartridge showing the bank continues behind the visible front row.

parts.name: Routed Expert Cartridge 10 of 64
parts.role: Rear-row expert cartridge for another independently routed SwiGLU shard.

parts.name: Routed Expert Cartridge 11 of 64
parts.role: Rear-row expert cartridge that makes all-to-all dispatch visually countable.

parts.name: Routed Expert Cartridge 12 of 64
parts.role: Rear-row expert cartridge showing the sparse expert pool beyond the top-3 active set.

parts.name: Routed Expert Cartridge 13 of 64
parts.role: Back-row expert cartridge anchoring the 4×4 exposed detail view of the 64-expert bank.

parts.name: Routed Expert Cartridge 14 of 64
parts.role: Back-row expert cartridge documenting another routed FFN shard.

parts.name: Routed Expert Cartridge 15 of 64
parts.role: Back-row expert cartridge for a capacity-factor-limited token route.

parts.name: Routed Expert Cartridge 16 of 64
parts.role: Back-row expert cartridge completing the visible 16-cartridge detail of the 64-routed-expert pool.

parts.name: 64-Expert Index Slab
parts.role: Transparent index plane declaring that the 16 exposed cartridges are a detail view of a 64-routed-expert bank.

parts.name: Shared Expert
parts.role: Always-on expert that handles common computation and over-capacity routed tokens.

parts.name: Expert Combine Bus
parts.role: All-to-all combine path that gathers top-3 expert outputs before writing back to the residual stream.

parts.name: MoE Residual Return Bus
parts.role: Visible return conduit carrying combined expert activations back from the MoE rail to the residual pipe.

parts.name: Projected FP4 Expert Weight Shelf
parts.role: Documents the projected FP4 or FP8 expert-weight quantization-aware training shelf for routed weights.

parts.name: Tied LM Head
parts.role: Projects the final residual state back to the projected 200K-token vocabulary using tied embedding weights.

parts.name: Next-Token Loss Probe
parts.role: Pre-training loss probe for next-token prediction before RL post-training.

parts.name: MARS Trainer Backplane
parts.role: Open top rail that makes the post-training loop separate from, but connected to, the base model.

parts.name: MARS Policy Swarm
parts.role: Projected multi-agent policy ring where copied policies debate or cooperate during long reasoning rollouts.
parts.algorithm: agents = [policy.copy() for _ in range(N)]; rollouts, debate_log = self_play(agents, prompts)

parts.name: Reward Model Bank
parts.role: Scores math, code, agentic tool-use, SWE, and debate-agreement outcomes for the projected MARS trainer.

parts.name: 200K-Token Rollout Buffer
parts.role: Stores projected long-output trajectories for RL updates over 200K-token reasoning traces.

parts.name: AdamW or Muon Optimizer Module
parts.role: Applies the projected RL and pre-training optimizer updates back into model weights.

parts.name: Trainer Feedback Bus
parts.role: Returns optimizer updates from the projected MARS loop to the model weights and residual stack.

parts.name: TP × EP × PP × DP Backplane
parts.role: Documents tensor, expert, pipeline, and data parallelism plus state-passing for chunked-scan lightning prefill.

parts.name: Parallelism Datum Bus
parts.role: Ground-level rail tying the rear parallelism panel physically back to the base frame and MoE assembly.

parts.name: 4M-Context Curriculum Pipe
parts.role: Represents projected pre-training and RL curriculum stages that extend input context to 4M tokens.
